font.reason: Vazir Code for Latin code chrome (monospace); Vazirmatn for the neutral UI labels and for the Persian comment letters, because the monospace face shows Persian as unjoined, spaced letters.

comps.translatedSummary: Two panels over the same syntax-highlighted code: line-by-line fade/rise (right) vs. char-by-char typing with block cursor (left). Labels: «ظهور خط‌به‌خط» / «تایپ حرف‌به‌حرف»; comment «// آماده».

rtlDecisions.why: First panel in reading order goes to the right half; both panels share one spec so x' = 100 - x - 45.
direction:rtl on the panel puts the label on the start (right) edge like an RTL UI header; letterSpacing/uppercase removed.
Code is an LTR island (direction:ltr, textAlign:left, isolate): syntax does not mirror and the cursor advances through the code in its own reading order.

rtlDecisions.what: translateY(8px) rise and top-to-bottom line stagger

rtlDecisions.why: Same 8 code points, so the 59-char typing pace and end frame are unchanged. Typed with prefix slicing: untyped remainder kept as hidden text for stable width, and ZWNJ between visible prefix and hidden rest so the last letter takes its right form; block cursor on last typed letter.

rtlDecisions.what: Token palette, easings, timings, seeds, block cursor colour
rtlDecisions.why: Motion fidelity; nothing in them depends on direction.

rasterTextHandling: No raster assets in this card.
concerns: Typing in the Persian comment starts at the right end of its RTL run and grows leftwards (natural Persian typing); the cursor block sits on the newest letter.
Code identifiers stay Latin by design (code syntax).
lessons: Monospace code fonts (Vazir Code) render Persian letters unjoined and spaced: switch Persian runs inside code to Vazirmatn (symptom: 'آ م ا د ه' with gaps).
Hidden-remainder typewriters in Persian: join into the invisible next letter gives a wrong medial form on the cursor letter; insert U+200C between the visible prefix and the hidden rest.
